{"m": "gpt-4o-mini", "msg": [{"content": "You compare short personal anecdotes by their underlying relational structure - the pattern of intentions, causes, deceptions, reversals, and outcomes among the people involved - NOT by their surface topic, setting, or vocabulary. Two stories can be about totally different situations yet share the same deep structure; two stories can share the same topic yet have opposite structure.", "role": "system"}, {"content": "SITUATION:
For five years I covered my brother's gambling debts, telling myself I was helping him through a rough patch. Each time I paid, he promised it was the last time. When he finally hit bottom—arrested for writing bad checks—his counselor said my bailouts had removed every consequence that might have forced him to seek help earlier. My support had funded his addiction.

CANDIDATE A:
I set clear boundaries with my brother about his gambling. I refused to cover his debts but paid for his addiction counseling directly. When he relapsed, I didn't bail him out—I drove him to his sponsor. The tough love was painful, but he's been in recovery for three years.

CANDIDATE B:
I let my aging father live alone because he insisted he was fine—I didn't want to hurt his pride. I brought groceries, cleaned when I visited, covered the bills he forgot. When he fell and lay alone for two days before anyone found him, I realized I'd been preserving his dignity at the cost of his safety. My respect had enabled his danger.

Which candidate shares the same underlying relational structure as the SITUATION (ignore surface topic similarity)? Respond as JSON: {"choice": "A" or "B", "reason": "<one sentence>"}.", "role": "user"}], "t": 0.0, "tag": "exp2:40"}
content: {"choice": "B", "reason": "Both stories involve enabling a loved one's harmful behavior under the guise of support, ultimately leading to negative consequences for the individual."}
